newsitem.title: USA: N.J. lawmaker proposes property tax relief.
newsitem.headline: N.J. lawmaker proposes property tax relief.

text.p: - The Speaker of New Jersey's Assembly Wednesday proposed a property tax relief program for middle-income senior citizens.
"It will make New Jersey better for all citizens, even though it applies to just one segment," Speaker Jack Collins, R-Salem, said.

Collins' plan would fix property tax liability at 1997 rates for people over 65 or who are disabled, and whose income is no more than $17,550, or $21,519 for married couples. Starting next year, the state would repay them for any tax increases imposed by local governments or school districts.
The nonpartisan Office of Legislative Services put the statewide average rise in property taxes at $152.

Collins estimated the cost to the treasury next year would be $18.4 million to cover claims from the 140,000 eligible taxpayers. But the cost will increase rapidly -- rising to $52 million in three years and $140 million in a decade, he said.
